claim: COH-3 is the most abundant kleisin on pachytene axial elements
source: This demonstrated that COH-3 is the most abundant kleisin on pachytene axial elements, which contain similar amounts of COH-4 and REC-8 (Figure 1B).
evidence: Quantification of fluorescent signal at axial elements in pachytene nuclei from strains with GFP-tagged kleisins, shown in Figure 1B

claim: Pachytene axial elements contain similar amounts of COH-4 and REC-8
source: This demonstrated that COH-3 is the most abundant kleisin on pachytene axial elements, which contain similar amounts of COH-4 and REC-8 (Figure 1B).
evidence: Quantification of fluorescent signal at axial elements shown in Figure 1B

claim: The ratio of COH-3/4 to REC-8 cohesin is 3.5
source: The ratio of COH-3/4 to REC-8 cohesin is 3.5, consistent with the observation that COH-3/4 cohesin plays a more prominent role than REC-8 cohesin in axis integrity of pachytene nuclei (Castellano-Pozo et al., 2020) and with previous estimations of REC-8 and COH-3/4 abundance on spread pachytene nuclei (Woglar et al., 2020).
evidence: Calculated from quantification data and consistent with previous studies

claim: COH-3/4 cohesin plays a more prominent role than REC-8 cohesin in axis integrity of pachytene nuclei
source: The ratio of COH-3/4 to REC-8 cohesin is 3.5, consistent with the observation that COH-3/4 cohesin plays a more prominent role than REC-8 cohesin in axis integrity of pachytene nuclei (Castellano-Pozo et al., 2020) and with previous estimations of REC-8 and COH-3/4 abundance on spread pachytene nuclei (Woglar et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Castellano-Pozo et al., 2020

claim: Continuous axial elements labelled by SMC-1::GFP were observed in wild-type controls and rec-8 mutants
source: Continuous axial elements labelled by SMC-1::GFP were observed in wild-type controls and rec-8 mutants, while SMC-1::GFP signals appeared as discontinuous weak signals in pachytene nuclei of coh-3 coh-4 double mutants (Figure 1C), in agreement with previous observations using SMC-3 antibodies (Severson and Meyer, 2014).
evidence: Structural illumination microscopy imaging shown in Figure 1C

claim: SMC-1::GFP signals appeared as discontinuous weak signals in pachytene nuclei of coh-3 coh-4 double mutants
source: Continuous axial elements labelled by SMC-1::GFP were observed in wild-type controls and rec-8 mutants, while SMC-1::GFP signals appeared as discontinuous weak signals in pachytene nuclei of coh-3 coh-4 double mutants (Figure 1C), in agreement with previous observations using SMC-3 antibodies (Severson and Meyer, 2014).
evidence: Structural illumination microscopy imaging shown in Figure 1C, consistent with previous observations

claim: SMC-1::GFP signal intensity was similar in wild-type controls and rec-8 mutants
source: SMC-1::GFP signal intensity was similar in wild-type controls and rec-8 mutants, while coh-3 coh-4 double mutants displayed a clear reduction in signal intensity (Figure 1D), confirming that in pachytene nuclei most SMC-1 is associated with COH-3/4 cohesin complexes.
evidence: Quantification of whole-nucleus mean intensity shown in Figure 1D

claim: coh-3 coh-4 double mutants displayed a clear reduction in SMC-1::GFP signal intensity
source: SMC-1::GFP signal intensity was similar in wild-type controls and rec-8 mutants, while coh-3 coh-4 double mutants displayed a clear reduction in signal intensity (Figure 1D), confirming that in pachytene nuclei most SMC-1 is associated with COH-3/4 cohesin complexes.
evidence: Quantification of whole-nucleus mean intensity shown in Figure 1D

claim: In pachytene nuclei most SMC-1 is associated with COH-3/4 cohesin complexes
source: SMC-1::GFP signal intensity was similar in wild-type controls and rec-8 mutants, while coh-3 coh-4 double mutants displayed a clear reduction in signal intensity (Figure 1D), confirming that in pachytene nuclei most SMC-1 is associated with COH-3/4 cohesin complexes.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that SMC-1 signal is reduced in coh-3 coh-4 mutants but not in rec-8 mutants

claim: COH-3/4 complexes are key regulators of higher-order chromosome organisation during meiotic prophase by ensuring the integrity of axial elements
source: Thus, by ensuring the integrity of axial elements, COH-3/4 complexes are key regulators of higher-order chromosome organisation during meiotic prophase.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that axial elements are discontinuous in coh-3 coh-4 mutants and that most SMC-1 is associated with COH-3/4

claim: REC-8::GFP shows very little recovery of axis-associated signal following photobleaching in pachytene nuclei
source: Following photobleaching of a small region of an axial element, we observed very little recovery of axis-associated REC-8::GFP signal, evidencing little reloading of REC-8::GFP over the imaging period (20 min) (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: FRAP analysis shown in Figure 1E

claim: COH-3::GFP and COH-4::GFP show recovery of fluorescence signal on photobleached axial elements, approaching 50% of pre-bleach levels over 20 min
source: In contrast, FRAP analysis of pachytene nuclei from coh-3::GFP coh-4::GFP homozygous worms demonstrated regaining of fluorescence signal on the photobleached region of the axis, which approached 50% of pre-bleach levels over 20 min (Figure 1F).
evidence: FRAP analysis shown in Figure 1F

claim: High-resolution FRAP demonstrated clear reloading of COH-3::mCherry, but not REC-8::GFP to axial elements of pachytene nuclei 10 min after photobleaching
source: Consistent with the full time-course experiment shown above, high-resolution FRAP demonstrated clear reloading of COH-3::mCherry, but not REC-8::GFP to axial elements of pachytene nuclei 10 min after photobleaching (Figure 1G and H).
evidence: High-resolution FRAP experiments shown in Figure 1G and H

claim: COH-3/4 complexes associate dynamically with pachytene axial elements
source: Thus, in contrast with REC-8 cohesin, COH-3/4 complexes associate dynamically with pachytene axial elements.
evidence: Inferred from FRAP experiments showing recovery of COH-3/4 signal but not REC-8 signal

claim: Only REC-8 complexes associate with chromosomes during meiotic S-phase, while COH-3/4 load post S-phase
source: In mammalian somatic cells, the creation of a stable pool of cohesin requires passage through S-phase (Gerlich et al., 2006) and in worms only REC-8 complexes associate with chromosomes during meiotic S-phase, while COH-3/4 load post S-phase (Severson and Meyer, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Severson and Meyer, 2014

claim: The different loading time of REC-8 and COH-3/4 cohesin may be a determinant of the dynamics of these complexes
source: Therefore, the different loading time of REC-8 and COH-3/4 cohesin may be a determinant of the dynamics of these complexes.
evidence: Speculative inference based on the observation that REC-8 loads during S-phase and is stable, while COH-3/4 loads post S-phase and is dynamic

claim: RAD21L complexes associate post S-phase during mouse meiosis
source: As RAD21L complexes also associate post S-phase during mouse meiosis (Ishiguro et al., 2014), our results suggest that, similar to COH-3/4, RAD21L may also associate dynamically with pachytene chromosomes.
evidence: Supported by citation to Ishiguro et al., 2014

claim: RAD21L may associate dynamically with pachytene chromosomes similar to COH-3/4
source: As RAD21L complexes also associate post S-phase during mouse meiosis (Ishiguro et al., 2014), our results suggest that, similar to COH-3/4, RAD21L may also associate dynamically with pachytene chromosomes.
evidence: Speculative inference based on similarity in loading time between RAD21L and COH-3/4

claim: In the absence of WAPL-1 the levels of axis-associated COH-3/4 are increased
source: In mammalian somatic cells, WAPL is required to maintain a pool of cohesin that associates dynamically with chromosomes (Tedeschi et al., 2013), and we have previously shown that in the absence of WAPL-1 the levels of axis-associated COH-3/4 are increased (Crawley et al., 2016), suggesting that WAPL-1 may control the dynamic association of COH-3/4 complexes.
evidence: Supported by citation to Crawley et al., 2016

claim: The dynamics of REC-8::GFP were similar in the presence and absence of WAPL-1, showing almost no increase of post-photobleaching fluorescence intensity
source: While the dynamics of REC-8::GFP were similar in the presence and absence of WAPL-1, showing almost no increase of post-photobleaching fluorescence intensity (Figure 2A), in the case of COH-3::GFP and COH-4::GFP the increase in post-photobleaching intensity was largely lost in the absence of WAPL-1 (Figure 2A).
evidence: FRAP analysis in wapl-1 mutants shown in Figure 2A

claim: In the absence of WAPL-1, the increase in post-photobleaching intensity of COH-3::GFP and COH-4::GFP was largely lost
source: While the dynamics of REC-8::GFP were similar in the presence and absence of WAPL-1, showing almost no increase of post-photobleaching fluorescence intensity (Figure 2A), in the case of COH-3::GFP and COH-4::GFP the increase in post-photobleaching intensity was largely lost in the absence of WAPL-1 (Figure 2A).
evidence: FRAP analysis in wapl-1 mutants shown in Figure 2A

claim: WAPL-1 is required to ensure the dynamic association of COH-3/4 cohesin with axial elements in pachytene nuclei
source: Therefore, WAPL-1 is required to ensure the dynamic association of COH-3/4 cohesin with axial elements in pachytene nuclei.
evidence: Inferred from FRAP experiments showing loss of COH-3/4 dynamics in wapl-1 mutants

claim: Removal of WAPL in mouse oocytes at the end of meiotic prophase results in increased binding of SCC1 cohesin, but not REC8 cohesin
source: Removal of WAPL in mouse oocytes at the end of meiotic prophase results in increased binding of SCC1 cohesin, but not REC8 cohesin (Silva et al., 2020), suggesting that REC8 cohesin is also largely refractory to WAPL-mediated removal during mammalian meiosis.
evidence: Supported by citation to Silva et al., 2020

claim: REC8 cohesin is largely refractory to WAPL-mediated removal during mammalian meiosis
source: Removal of WAPL in mouse oocytes at the end of meiotic prophase results in increased binding of SCC1 cohesin, but not REC8 cohesin (Silva et al., 2020), suggesting that REC8 cohesin is also largely refractory to WAPL-mediated removal during mammalian meiosis.
evidence: Inferred from observations in mouse oocytes cited from Silva et al., 2020

claim: The establishment of a population of cohesin that is refractory to the removal activity of WAPL may be a conserved feature of the meiotic programme
source: Thus, the establishment of a population of cohesin that is refractory to the removal activity of WAPL may be a conserved feature of the meiotic programme.
evidence: Inferred from observations in both C. elegans and mouse showing REC-8 cohesin is refractory to WAPL

claim: SCC-2 is required for the initial loading of COH-3/4 cohesin
source: We first verified that SCC-2 is indeed required for the initial loading of COH-3/4 cohesin (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) as previous studies only assessed this indirectly by monitoring SMC-1 loading (Lightfoot et al., 2011).
evidence: Immunostaining shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A

claim: SCC-2 depletion for 8 hr induced a reduction of 35% of COH-3/4 signal intensity in mid pachytene nuclei that underwent meiotic S-phase before the start of auxin treatment
source: Staining of auxin-treated germlines with anti-COH-3/4 antibodies showed that SCC-2 depletion for 8 hr induced a reduction of 35% of COH-3/4 signal intensity (quantified as whole-nucleus mean intensity) in mid pachytene nuclei that underwent meiotic S-phase before the start of auxin treatment (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Quantification of COH-3/4 signal after auxin-mediated SCC-2 depletion shown in Figure 2B

claim: COH-3/4 signal intensity in mid pachytene nuclei was reduced to 48% of untreated controls following 14 hr of auxin treatment
source: COH-3/4 signal intensity in mid pachytene nuclei was further reduced to 48% of untreated controls following 14 hr of auxin treatment (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Quantification of COH-3/4 signal after auxin-mediated SCC-2 depletion shown in Figure 2B

claim: SCC-2 depletion resulted in only a moderate decrease (9%) of REC-8 signal intensity in mid pachytene nuclei after 14 hr of auxin treatment
source: In contrast, SCC-2 depletion resulted in only a moderate decrease (9%) of REC-8 signal intensity in mid pachytene nuclei after 14 hr of auxin treatment (Figure 2B).
evidence: Quantification of REC-8 signal after auxin-mediated SCC-2 depletion shown in Figure 2B

claim: SCC-2 is required for maintaining the levels of chromosome-bound COH-3/4, but not REC-8, cohesin in pachytene nuclei
source: These findings show that SCC-2 is required for maintaining the levels of chromosome-bound COH-3/4, but not REC-8, cohesin in pachytene nuclei.
evidence: Inferred from differential effects of SCC-2 depletion on COH-3/4 versus REC-8 levels

claim: When SCC-2 was depleted from pachytene nuclei of wapl-1 RNAi worms, COH-3/4 levels were not reduced compared to untreated (empty RNAi, no auxin) worms
source: When SCC-2 was depleted from pachytene nuclei of wapl-1 RNAi worms, COH-3/4 levels were not reduced compared to untreated (empty RNAi, no auxin) worms (Figure 2C), consistent with SCC-2 and WAPL-1 having antagonistic loading and unloading activities in pachytene nuclei.
evidence: Quantification of COH-3/4 levels in wapl-1 RNAi worms with SCC-2 depletion shown in Figure 2C

claim: SCC-2 and WAPL-1 have antagonistic loading and unloading activities in pachytene nuclei
source: When SCC-2 was depleted from pachytene nuclei of wapl-1 RNAi worms, COH-3/4 levels were not reduced compared to untreated (empty RNAi, no auxin) worms (Figure 2C), consistent with SCC-2 and WAPL-1 having antagonistic loading and unloading activities in pachytene nuclei.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that SCC-2 depletion does not reduce COH-3/4 levels in the absence of WAPL-1

claim: SCC-2 may act to prevent WAPL-1-independent removal of COH-3/4 complexes
source: This suggests that that in addition to promoting loading of COH-3/4 complexes removed by WAPL-1, SCC-2 may also act to prevent WAPL-1-independent removal of COH-3/4 complexes.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that SCC-2 depletion in wapl-1 RNAi worms results in lower COH-3/4 levels than wapl-1 RNAi alone

claim: Mouse NIPBL (SCC2) localises to axial elements of pachytene nuclei
source: Similar to worms, mouse NIPBL (SCC2) also localises to axial elements of pachytene nuclei (Kuleszewicz et al., 2013), suggesting that cohesin turnover during pachytene, presumably of non-cohesive RAD21L complexes, may be a conserved feature of meiosis.
evidence: Supported by citation to Kuleszewicz et al., 2013

claim: Cohesin turnover during pachytene, presumably of non-cohesive RAD21L complexes, may be a conserved feature of meiosis
source: Similar to worms, mouse NIPBL (SCC2) also localises to axial elements of pachytene nuclei (Kuleszewicz et al., 2013), suggesting that cohesin turnover during pachytene, presumably of non-cohesive RAD21L complexes, may be a conserved feature of meiosis.
evidence: Speculative inference based on similarity between worm and mouse SCC-2/NIPBL localization

claim: TEV-mediated removal of REC-8::GFP caused partial disassembly of diakinesis bivalents, which in most cases appeared as four lobed structures
source: TEV-mediated removal of REC-8::GFP caused partial disassembly of diakinesis bivalents, which in most cases appeared as four lobed structures that remained weakly connected at the crossover site, with each lobe likely corresponding to one of the four chromatids present in a bivalent (Figure 3A).
evidence: Imaging of diakinesis oocytes after TEV-mediated REC-8 removal shown in Figure 3A

claim: TEV-mediated REC-8 removal resulted in 35% of oocytes displaying individual chromatids that were fully detached
source: In addition to lobed bivalents, TEV-mediated REC-8 removal resulted in 35% of oocytes displaying individual chromatids that were fully detached (Figure 3A).
evidence: Quantification of diakinesis oocyte morphology after TEV-mediated REC-8 removal shown in Figure 3A

claim: COH-3 and condensin II remained bound to diakinesis chromosomes following REC-8 removal, including on fully detached chromatids
source: Importantly, visualisation of COH-3 and condensin II confirmed that these SMC complexes remained bound to diakinesis chromosomes following REC-8 removal, including on fully detached chromatids (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: Immunostaining of COH-3 and condensin II after REC-8 removal shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and C

claim: The observed disruption in SCC following REC-8 removal is specifically caused by the loss of REC-8 and not by an indirect effect of REC-8 removal on other SMC complexes
source: Therefore, the observed disruption in SCC is specifically caused by the loss of REC-8 and not by an indirect effect of REC-8 removal on other SMC complexes.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that other SMC complexes remain bound after REC-8 removal

claim: COH-3/4 complexes associate with individual chromatids and therefore do not partake in SCC
source: The fact that COH-3 remains associated with fully detached chromatids following REC-8 removal in diakinesis oocytes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C) suggests that COH-3/4 complexes associate with individual chromatids and therefore do not partake in SCC.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that COH-3 remains on detached chromatids after REC-8 removal

claim: TEV-mediated removal of COH-3 or the mitotic kleisin SCC-1 caused no obvious morphological changes in diakinesis bivalents
source: Indeed, TEV-mediated removal of COH-3 or the mitotic kleisin SCC-1, which also associates with meiotic prophase chromosomes (Severson and Meyer, 2014), caused no obvious morphological changes in diakinesis bivalents (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D), consistent with COH-3/4 or SCC-1 not providing SCC in diakinesis oocytes.
evidence: Imaging of diakinesis oocytes after TEV-mediated COH-3 or SCC-1 removal shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D

claim: COH-3/4 or SCC-1 do not provide SCC in diakinesis oocytes
source: Indeed, TEV-mediated removal of COH-3 or the mitotic kleisin SCC-1, which also associates with meiotic prophase chromosomes (Severson and Meyer, 2014), caused no obvious morphological changes in diakinesis bivalents (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D), consistent with COH-3/4 or SCC-1 not providing SCC in diakinesis oocytes.
evidence: Inferred from the lack of morphological changes after COH-3 or SCC-1 removal

claim: REC-8 removal from diakinesis oocytes of spo-11 mutants induced a more penetrant loss of SCC
source: In this case, REC-8 removal induced a more penetrant loss of SCC (Figure 3C), suggesting that a recombination-dependent feature of chromosome organisation is involved in the weak chromatid connections observed when REC-8 is removed from diakinesis bivalents.
evidence: Imaging of spo-11 mutant diakinesis oocytes after REC-8 removal shown in Figure 3C

claim: A recombination-dependent feature of chromosome organisation is involved in the weak chromatid connections observed when REC-8 is removed from diakinesis bivalents
source: In this case, REC-8 removal induced a more penetrant loss of SCC (Figure 3C), suggesting that a recombination-dependent feature of chromosome organisation is involved in the weak chromatid connections observed when REC-8 is removed from diakinesis bivalents.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that REC-8 removal causes more complete loss of SCC in spo-11 mutants

claim: SCC remained intact following COH-3 removal in diakinesis bivalents of spo-11 mutants
source: We also tested a possible role of COH-3 in mediating SCC in diakinesis bivalents of spo-11 mutants, but in this case, SCC remained intact following COH-3 removal (Figure 3D).
evidence: Imaging of spo-11 mutant diakinesis oocytes after COH-3 removal shown in Figure 3D

claim: SCC is exclusively provided by REC-8 complexes in diakinesis oocytes
source: These results suggest that SCC is exclusively provided by REC-8 complexes in diakinesis oocytes.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that only REC-8 removal, not COH-3 removal, causes loss of SCC

claim: Removal of REC-8 from metaphase I-arrested oocytes caused a general loss of SCC, with most oocytes displaying between 17 and 24 DAPI-stained bodies
source: Removal of REC-8 from metaphase I-arrested oocytes caused a general loss of SCC, with most oocytes displaying between 17 and 24 DAPI-stained bodies (full loss of SCC would result in 24 chromatids), while six bivalents remained present following COH-3 or SCC-1 removal (Figure 3E and F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: Imaging of metaphase I oocytes after REC-8 removal shown in Figure 3E

claim: Six bivalents remained present following COH-3 or SCC-1 removal from metaphase I-arrested oocytes
source: Removal of REC-8 from metaphase I-arrested oocytes caused a general loss of SCC, with most oocytes displaying between 17 and 24 DAPI-stained bodies (full loss of SCC would result in 24 chromatids), while six bivalents remained present following COH-3 or SCC-1 removal (Figure 3E and F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: Imaging of metaphase I oocytes after COH-3 or SCC-1 removal shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1F

claim: SCC is exclusively provided by REC-8 cohesin in metaphase I oocytes of C. elegans
source: Regardless, the clear conclusion from our temporally resolved kleisin removal experiments is that, similar to mouse oocytes (Tachibana-Konwalski et al., 2010), SCC is exclusively provided by REC-8 cohesin in metaphase I oocytes of C. elegans.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that only REC-8 removal causes loss of SCC in metaphase I oocytes

claim: Removal of REC-8, but not of COH-3 or SCC-1, caused loss of SCC in late pachytene nuclei
source: Imaging of HIM-8 foci in late pachytene nuclei demonstrated that removal of REC-8, but not of COH-3 or SCC-1, caused loss of SCC (Figure 3G).
evidence: Imaging of HIM-8 foci in late pachytene nuclei after kleisin removal shown in Figure 3G

claim: SCC is provided by REC-8 complexes in pachytene nuclei
source: These observations suggest that SCC is provided by REC-8 complexes in pachytene nuclei, consistent with a model in which complexes that provide SCC are stably bound to chromosomes between DNA replication and the onset of the meiotic divisions (Burkhardt et al., 2016).
evidence: Inferred from the observation that only REC-8 removal causes loss of SCC in pachytene nuclei

claim: SCC-2 is not required for maintaining REC-8 on pachytene chromosomes
source: The stable association of cohesion-providing REC-8 complexes with meiotic chromosomes is also supported by our findings that SCC-2 is not required for maintaining REC-8 on pachytene chromosomes (Figure 2B and E).
evidence: Data from SCC-2 depletion experiments shown in Figure 2B

claim: Both REC-8 and SCC remained intact in diakinesis oocytes after 14 hr of auxin-mediated SCC-2 depletion
source: Moreover, we found that both REC-8 and SCC remained intact in diakinesis oocytes after 14 hr of auxin-mediated SCC-2 depletion (Figure 3H).
evidence: Imaging of diakinesis oocytes after SCC-2 depletion shown in Figure 3H

claim: Maintenance of normal levels of COH-3/4 complexes requires SCC-2 in pachytene nuclei
source: In contrast, maintenance of normal levels of COH-3/4 complexes, presumably associated with individual chromatids, does require SCC-2 in pachytene nuclei (see Figure 2B).
evidence: Data from SCC-2 depletion experiments shown in Figure 2B

claim: Extensive chromosome fragmentation was evident in diakinesis oocytes of irradiated rec-8 mutants, with around 40% of the DAPI-stained bodies displaying a surface area consistent with chromosome fragments
source: In contrast, extensive chromosome fragmentation was evident in diakinesis oocytes of irradiated rec-8 mutants, with around 40% of the DAPI-stained bodies displaying a surface area consistent with chromosome fragments (Figure 4A).
evidence: Quantification of chromosome fragmentation in irradiated rec-8 mutants shown in Figure 4A

claim: Chromosome fragmentation was detected in diakinesis oocytes of irradiated coh-3 coh-4 double mutants, although to a much lesser extent than in rec-8 mutants
source: Chromosome fragmentation was also detected in diakinesis oocytes of irradiated coh-3 coh-4 double mutants, although to a much lesser extent than in rec-8 mutants.
evidence: Quantification of chromosome fragmentation in irradiated coh-3 coh-4 mutants shown in Figure 4A

claim: Late pachytene nuclei of irradiated rec-8 mutants contained high numbers of RAD-51 foci, evidencing impaired DSB repair
source: In contrast, late pachytene nuclei of irradiated rec-8 mutants contained high numbers of RAD-51 foci, evidencing impaired DSB repair (Figure 4B).
evidence: Quantification of RAD-51 foci in irradiated rec-8 mutants shown in Figure 4B

claim: SCC-providing REC-8 complexes play a more prominent role in DSB repair than non-cohesive, dynamically bound, COH-3/4 complexes
source: Thus, SCC-providing REC-8 complexes appear to play a more prominent role in DSB repair than non-cohesive, dynamically bound, COH-3/4 complexes.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that rec-8 mutants show more severe DSB repair defects than coh-3 coh-4 mutants

claim: Double mutants lacking REC-8 and SC components display a striking accumulation of RAD-51 foci that persisted into diakinesis oocytes
source: Supporting this possibility, double mutants lacking REC-8 and SC components display a striking accumulation of RAD-51 foci that persisted into diakinesis oocytes (Cahoon et al., 2019; Figure 4C).
evidence: Quantification of RAD-51 foci in rec-8 syp-2 double mutants shown in Figure 4C

claim: rec-8 syp-2 double mutant germlines display elongated RAD-51 structures (stretches)
source: In addition to high numbers of regular size RAD-51 foci, rec-8 syp-2 double mutant germlines also display elongated RAD-51 structures (stretches) (Figure 4C), suggesting the presence of abnormal recombination intermediates.
evidence: Imaging of RAD-51 in rec-8 syp-2 double mutants shown in Figure 4C

claim: RAD-51 foci gradually decrease during late pachytene of coh-3 coh-4 syp-2 triple mutant germlines and are largely lacking in diplotene and diakinesis oocytes
source: In contrast to rec-8 syp-2 double mutants, RAD-51 foci gradually decrease during late pachytene of coh-3 coh-4 syp-2 triple mutant germlines and are largely lacking in diplotene and diakinesis oocytes (Figure 4C), consistent with the lack of chromosome fragments in oocytes of these mutants (Crawley et al., 2016).
evidence: Quantification of RAD-51 foci in coh-3 coh-4 syp-2 triple mutants shown in Figure 4C

claim: Removing the SC from mutants lacking COH-3/4 cohesin does not compromise DSB repair
source: Thus, removing the SC from mutants lacking COH-3/4 cohesin does not compromise DSB repair, suggesting that inter-sister DSB repair mediated by REC-8 cohesin is sufficient to repair SPO-11 DSBs that accumulate in the absence of SC.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that coh-3 coh-4 syp-2 triple mutants show efficient DSB repair

claim: Inter-sister DSB repair mediated by REC-8 cohesin is sufficient to repair SPO-11 DSBs that accumulate in the absence of SC
source: Thus, removing the SC from mutants lacking COH-3/4 cohesin does not compromise DSB repair, suggesting that inter-sister DSB repair mediated by REC-8 cohesin is sufficient to repair SPO-11 DSBs that accumulate in the absence of SC.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that coh-3 coh-4 syp-2 triple mutants show efficient DSB repair

claim: SCC-providing REC-8 complexes play a much more prominent role in the repair of endogenous (SPO-11-dependent) and exogenous (IR) DSBs during late meiotic prophase
source: Therefore, although COH-3/4 complexes are much more abundant than REC-8 complexes and are essential for the integrity of axial elements (Figure 1B and C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), SCC-providing REC-8 complexes play a much more prominent role in the repair of endogenous (SPO-11-dependent) and exogenous (IR) DSBs during late meiotic prophase.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that rec-8 mutants show more severe DSB repair defects than coh-3 coh-4 mutants

claim: The role of REC-8 in DSB repair during meiotic prophase is mechanistically coupled to its ability to provide SCC
source: Our results suggest that similar to yeast Scc1 cohesin during mitotic G2 (Sjögren and Nasmyth, 2001), the role of REC-8 in DSB repair during meiotic prophase is mechanistically coupled to its ability to provide SCC.
evidence: Speculative inference based on similarity to yeast Scc1 cohesin

claim: REC-8 complexes loaded during meiotic S-phase tether sister chromatids until the meiotic divisions
source: Our studies support a model in which REC-8 complexes loaded during meiotic S-phase tether sister chromatids until the meiotic divisions, while COH-3/4 loaded post S-phase on individual chromatids act to control higher-order chromosome structure, likely by performing loop extrusion (Figure 5).
evidence: Model based on integration of all experimental findings

claim: COH-3/4 loaded post S-phase on individual chromatids act to control higher-order chromosome structure, likely by performing loop extrusion
source: Our studies support a model in which REC-8 complexes loaded during meiotic S-phase tether sister chromatids until the meiotic divisions, while COH-3/4 loaded post S-phase on individual chromatids act to control higher-order chromosome structure, likely by performing loop extrusion (Figure 5).
evidence: Model based on integration of all experimental findings, with loop extrusion being speculative

claim: During meiosis in higher eukaryotes, SCC and loop extrusion activities can be determined by kleisin identity
source: How different populations of Scc1 cohesin are regulated to perform either SCC or loop extrusion is not understood, but our findings suggest that during meiosis in higher eukaryotes these activities can be determined by kleisin identity.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that REC-8 and COH-3/4 complexes have distinct functions

claim: Cohesin plays essential roles in chromosome segregation, 3D genome organisation, and DNA damage repair through its ability to modify DNA topology
source: The cohesin complex plays essential roles in chromosome segregation, 3D genome organisation, and DNA damage repair through its ability to modify DNA topology.
evidence: General statement about cohesin function based on established knowledge

claim: In higher eukaryotes, meiotic chromosome function requires cohesin complexes containing meiosis-specific kleisin subunits: REC8 and RAD21L in mammals and REC-8 and COH-3/4 in Caenorhabditis elegans
source: In higher eukaryotes, meiotic chromosome function, and therefore fertility, requires cohesin complexes containing meiosis-specific kleisin subunits: REC8 and RAD21L in mammals and REC-8 and COH-3/4 in Caenorhabditis elegans.
evidence: General statement about meiotic kleisins based on established knowledge

claim: REC-8 complexes provide sister chromatid cohesion (SCC) and DNA repair
source: Combining time-resolved methods of protein removal with live imaging and exploiting the temporospatial organisation of the C. elegans germline, we show that REC-8 complexes provide sister chromatid cohesion (SCC) and DNA repair, while COH-3/4 complexes control higher-order chromosome structure.
evidence: Summary of main findings from the study

claim: COH-3/4 complexes control higher-order chromosome structure
source: Combining time-resolved methods of protein removal with live imaging and exploiting the temporospatial organisation of the C. elegans germline, we show that REC-8 complexes provide sister chromatid cohesion (SCC) and DNA repair, while COH-3/4 complexes control higher-order chromosome structure.
evidence: Summary of main findings from the study

claim: Functional conservation may extend to worm and mouse REC8 cohesin, with these complexes providing SCC and being largely refractory to WAPL-mediated removal in both organisms
source: Our studies suggest functional conservation between worm and mouse REC8 cohesin, with these complexes providing SCC and being largely refractory to WAPL-mediated removal in both organisms (Crawley et al., 2016; Silva et al., 2020; Tachibana-Konwalski et al., 2010).
evidence: Inference based on comparison of findings in worms with published studies in mice

claim: Mammalian RAD21L complexes may associate dynamically with meiotic chromosomes in a manner regulated by WAPL and NIPBL
source: Moreover, as we provide evidence suggesting that functional conservation may also extend to COH-3/4-RAD21L complexes, we hypothesise that, similar to C. elegans COH-3/4, mammalian RAD21L complexes may associate dynamically with meiotic chromosomes in a manner regulated by WAPL and NIPBL.
evidence: Speculative hypothesis based on similarity between COH-3/4 and RAD21L

claim: In somatic cells, cohesin ensures correct chromosome segregation by providing sister chromatid cohesion (SCC) between S-phase and the onset of anaphase
source: In somatic cells, cohesin ensures correct chromosome segregation by providing sister chromatid cohesion (SCC) between S-phase and the onset of anaphase, ensures genome stability through its role in DNA damage repair, and regulates gene expression by controlling genome folding through DNA looping.
evidence: General statement about cohesin function in somatic cells based on established knowledge

claim: During meiosis, cohesin orchestrates the formation of proteinaceous axial elements that promote pairing and recombination between homologous chromosomes
source: In addition, during meiosis, cohesin orchestrates the formation of proteinaceous axial elements that promote pairing and recombination between homologous chromosomes and facilitates the two-step release of SCC during the consecutive meiotic divisions (Klein et al., 1999; Grey and de Massy, 2021).
evidence: General statement about cohesin function in meiosis supported by citations

claim: The correct function of meiotic cohesin is essential for fertility
source: As inter-homologue recombination and the step-wise release of SCC are prerequisites for the formation of euploid gametes (Petronczki et al., 2003), the correct function of meiotic cohesin is essential for fertility.
